gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the UGREEN DXP6800 Pro, ChatGPT's 'favorite all-in-one', splits its six bays across two SATA controllers (Intel Alder Lake-P AHCI at 00:17.0 plus an ASMedia ASM1164), while the DXP4800 Plus puts all four bays on a single ASM1164, so a TrueNAS VM under Proxmox gets every bay with one passthrough on the 4800 Plus but needs two on the 6800 Pro.
standout_why: Here is what the rival pages say. proxmox.com/requirements (cited in all 3 chats) only says 'For PCI(e) passthrough a CPU with VT-d or AMD-Vi CPU flag is required'. It says nothing about IOMMU groups or which controller each NAS uses. homelabpicks.com covers IOMMU grouping only in general terms ('SATA controller passthrough to a TrueNAS VM depends on IOMMU grouping on your unit'), names no SATA chip and doesn't cover UGREEN. computingforgeeks.com/best-nas-for-proxmox covers the DXP6800 Pro but never mentions passthrough, IOMMU or a watchdog. ChatGPT's own answers stop at 'pass through the disk controller where hardware and IOMMU groups permit'. None of these pages mentions UGREEN's BIOS watchdog. Our own current page already has the watchdog line and the DXP8800 Plus 'only one of two controllers passes through' point, but it says nothing about the DXP6800 Pro split or the DXP4800 Plus single-controller layout. I scored it 2 rather than 3 because the DXP6800 Pro split rests on one owner's lspci plus a mapping in a community LED project, not on UGREEN's spec sheet.
decides: If the shopper's plan is Proxmox bare-metal with a TrueNAS VM that owns the drives, the DXP4800 Plus is the clean fit: one ASM1164 holds all 4 bays, and an owner passed it from the Proxmox GUI. On the DXP6800 Pro (and the DXP8800 Plus) one controller passthrough covers only some of the bays. You either pass both controllers, fall back to per-disk passthrough (an owner saw TrueNAS SCALE refuse a RAIDZ because the vDisks lacked unique serials), or let Proxmox run ZFS itself. On any UGREEN, the BIOS watchdog has to be turned off first or the box reboots about every 3 minutes without UGOS.

findings.label: SATA controller serving the 4 bays
findings.value: 1× ASMedia ASM1164 AHCI (PCI 04:00.0, 1b21:1164); bays 1–4 = ata1–ata4; no Intel 00:17.0 SATA controller listed
findings.source_title: Model report: DXP4800 Plus / Pro · Issue #266 · ugreen-nas-control
findings.note: Owner hardware report by ivolution, opened 2026-11-07, BIOS AMI 5.27 dated 01/09/2025. The lspci output shows only one SATA controller. The two M.2 slots hang off CPU root ports 00:06.0 and 00:06.2, separate from the SATA controller, so a Proxmox boot NVMe stays with the host when the SATA controller is passed through. The report doesn't list IOMMU group numbers.

findings.label: Owner-reported TrueNAS-in-Proxmox controller passthrough
findings.value: All HDDs on one SATA controller, passed to a TrueNAS VM from the Proxmox GUI; disks and smartd visible in TrueNAS; VM given 16 GB RAM with ballooning off
findings.source_title: NAS UGreen DXP4800 Plus | Proxmox Support Forum
findings.note: Post #8 by elvito, 2025-12-05: 'Die HDDs hängen beim 4800er an einem Sata Controller den man bequem in der Proxmox Gui an die Truenas VM durchreichen kann.' In the same post, about the DXP8800 Plus: 'beim 8800er lässt sich aktuell nur ein Sata Controller durchreichen'.

findings.label: SATA controllers present
findings.value: 2: Intel Alder Lake-P SATA AHCI (00:17.0, 8086:51d3) and ASMedia ASM1164 AHCI (5e:00.0, 1b21:1164)
findings.source_title: IOMMU/DMAR Regression (PTE Write access) on Alder Lake-P (Ugreen DXP6800 Pro) | Proxmox Support Forum
findings.note: lspci posted by wuselfaktor on 2026-03-28 on Proxmox VE 9.1.6. They were passing SATA through VFIO to a TrueNAS SCALE VM.

findings.label: Bay-to-host-adapter mapping
findings.value: SCSI hosts 0:0:0:0 and 1:0:0:0 = disk5 and disk6; hosts 2:0:0:0 to 6:0:0:0 = disk1 to disk4
findings.source_title: miskcoo/ugreen_leds_controller: An LED Controller for UGREEN's DX/DXP NAS Series
findings.note: The project says 'The HCTL mapping depends on how the SATA controllers are connected to the PCIe bus and the disk slots.' Reading this together with the two-controller lspci above, bays 5–6 and bays 1–4 sit behind different host adapters. That makes it likely that one passed-through controller gives a TrueNAS VM only some of the 6 bays. This is inferred from the mapping; neither source states the controller-to-bay pairing outright.

findings.label: Kernel-dependent passthrough fault on the ASM1164
findings.value: 'DMAR: [DMA Write NO_PASID] Request device [5e:00.0] … PTE Write access is not set' on kernel 6.17.13-2-pve; works on 6.17.9-1-pve; works on 7.0.14-19-pve without intel_iommu=sp_off (lwysocki, 2026-10-04, PVE 9.2.21)
findings.source_title: IOMMU/DMAR Regression (PTE Write access) on Alder Lake-P (Ugreen DXP6800 Pro) | Proxmox Support Forum
findings.note: Two workarounds were reported in the thread: pinning the older kernel, or adding intel_iommu=sp_off (CycloneB on 2026-07-26, wuselfaktor on 2026-07-31). CycloneB filed it as Proxmox Bugzilla 7505 on 2026-04-19.

findings.label: Proxmox rule for passthrough
findings.value: 'For working PCI passthrough, you need a dedicated IOMMU group for all PCI devices you want to assign to a VM.' ACS override 'should be seen as a last option'. A passed device 'is not available to the host anymore'
findings.note: Project's own words. They explain why the per-model controller layout above decides the TrueNAS-VM plan.

findings.label: BIOS watchdog under a non-UGOS OS
findings.value: Reboots the NAS about every 3 minutes if UGOS is not detected, unless Watchdog Control is disabled in BIOS (Advanced > Watchdog Settings; on i5 models possibly the 'FAST' tab)
findings.source_title: TrueNAS on a UGREEN NAS – INSTALLATION GUIDE – NAS Compares
findings.note: Named reviewer Rob Andrews (NAS Compares), 2024-07-11. Disabling it 'prevent[s] the system from rebooting every 3 minutes if UGOS is not detected'. Proxmox forum user celemine1gig (2026-02-03, thread 180160) says the DXP6800 Pro watchdog is handled by the in-kernel it87_wdt module if someone wants to re-enable it under Proxmox.

findings.label: Proxmox's own hardware requirement for passthrough
findings.value: 'For PCI(e) passthrough a CPU with VT-d or AMD-Vi CPU flag is required.' 'Neither ZFS nor Ceph are compatible with a hardware RAID controller.'
findings.note: This is the rival page ChatGPT cited in all three chats. I'm including it to show its baseline: it never mentions IOMMU groups or per-NAS controller layouts.

unsourced: UGREEN's own wording on the BIOS watchdog and third-party OS. ai.ugreen.com/pages/service returned HTTP 429 twice and support.ugnas.com/detail/article/en-US/133 rendered no text, so the watchdog interval comes from NAS Compares, not UGREEN.
IOMMU group number for the ASM1164 on the DXP4800 Plus and DXP6800 Pro. The issue #266 report and the Proxmox threads give lspci output but no /sys/kernel/iommu_groups listing.
An explicit statement of which DXP6800 Pro bays are wired to the Intel SATA controller and which to the ASM1164. I only have the HCTL host mapping from the LED project plus the two-controller lspci.
ASMedia's own ASM1164 spec page (port count, PCIe lanes). The ASMedia URL I opened was the ASM1064, and a search didn't surface the ASM1164 page.
SATA controller layout and Proxmox passthrough reports for the QNAP TVS-h674 and Minisforum N5 Pro. I didn't reach them within the tool budget.
